findings.text: The fragment states 'The four 550-cell H200 cases were never run' and the parity table at line 47 records 'not run / cut from the allocation', but logs/parity.log:1 names job 1307768 running tests/test_bank_step_booking_batch.py::test_shared_ring_geometry_matches_per_direction and its last lines read '4 failed in 722.95s' and 'EXIT=1': all four cases ran and failed, a ValueError in assert_peak_scaled_equal reshaping 1650x1650 into (1650,3,550,1650), which is the node's own helper. The record therefore reports an attempted-and-failed gate as never attempted, which is the one state a coordinator cannot audit.

The done_when requires the base-against-head table to carry assembly device ms per call and launches per call beside wall, reads, updates and peak memory; the timing table carries neither, and grep over the whole fragment finds no launch count and no assembly device time, because the stage split that would have produced them never ran. The figure at line 15 plots solve wall per slice against batch width, not the assembly device ms per stage at 16 and 128 slices the brief specifies.

The precision sentence says 'the three geometry ratios at most 2.59e-5 against 1e-8 for flux and 5e-4 for the axis and the saddle', which reads as a 2.59e-5 value being compared against a 1e-8 bound; the instrument at scripts/prototypes/bank_batch_width/measure.py:154-167 measures axis, saddle and boundary only, so the flux-within-1e-8 lane of the locked budget is never computed and the 'every lane inside the budget' claim rests on three of four lanes.

The job's final line is printf 'EXIT=%s\n' "$ROOT", which prints the tree path where the exit code belongs; logs/head2-1307761.log holds the single line 'EXIT=/home/ITER/mcintos/Code/.reckon-worktrees/...', so the head suite job's overall status cannot be read from its log by the receipt reader the rest of the run's machinery assumes.

This paired base/head suite runner duplicates the capability scripts/prototypes/../bank_matrix_free_step/suites.sh already owns (base and head arms, one fresh pytest process per file, separate basetemp, EXIT= last line), differing only in a hardcoded file list and an SBATCH header; it should have been extended rather than copied, and the copy is where the head arm's broken EXIT line above came from.

As added at 461641d1f the CPU parity test scaled by one global peak (peak = np.max(np.abs(rebuilt)); gap = max|shared-rebuilt| / peak) instead of the per-row peak_scaled_gap the brief names and that the same file's assert_peak_scaled_equal imports, so a small row's error is divided by the largest entry anywhere in the matrix; this weakens exactly the comparison the negative control was run against.
